core_obligations: Record that geometric normality at x implies the condition on finite purely inseparable base changes (proof line 2135).

From that condition to geometric normality of the local ring: the tensor product of O_{X,x} with a finite purely inseparable extension is local with the same spectrum, so it is the local ring at the unique point above x, and normality there plus the algebra characterization gives the conclusion (proof lines 2135-2146).

Back to geometric normality at x: for an arbitrary field extension, surjectivity of the base change gives a point above x whose local ring is a localization of the tensor product, hence normal (proof lines 2149-2156).
proof_roadmap: Second to third via uniqueness of the lifted point (proof lines 2135-2146).
Third to first via localization of the tensor product (proof lines 2149-2156).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over k and a point x, the lemma proves the equivalence of geometric normality at x, normality of the local rings at all points above x after every finite purely inseparable base change, and geometric normality of the local ring O_{X,x} over k (statement lines 2117-2132). The proof mirrors the geometric regularity case: from the second condition the author observes that the spectrum of O_{X,x} tensor_k k' agrees with that of O_{X,x} for a finite purely inseparable extension, so the tensor product is local and is the local ring at the unique point above x, which normality of that ring plus the algebra characterization turns into geometric normality of the local ring (proof lines 2135-2146). In the other direction an arbitrary field extension is handled by surjectivity of the base change, which produces a point x' above x whose local ring is a localization of O_{X,x} tensor_k k', hence normal by assumption (proof lines 2149-2156). The claim is H2: the uniqueness of the lifted point under a purely inseparable extension is the key input, and the two directions are otherwise short.
